p.fact: This project builds a tool that manages itself — a self-updating CLI, an installer, a version manager, or a package system.
The **tool design lessons** catalog is installed: numbered, self-contained lessons, each one paid for by shipping such a tool and the ecosystem around it.
Before you design an activation model, an install pipeline, an identity scheme, a durable-environment edit, or a package format, read the lesson that governs it **first**.
The law is one line; the rationale is why it is not negotiable.

item.fact: Packaging — what ships, what identity is, the bootstrap: @spec://org.vibevm.world/tool-design-lessons/flows/tool-design-lessons/packaging-lessons#root.

p.fact: The index and the cross-cutting maxims: @spec://org.vibevm.world/tool-design-lessons/flows/tool-design-lessons/TOOL-DESIGN-LESSONS#root.

item.fact: Never make an environment variable the source of truth for the active version — env is frozen at process start; read a live pointer file each launch instead.
Never overwrite a file that may be in use — write a new instance directory and flip a pointer.
Never content-hash gigabytes to establish identity — count instances and detect change cheaply.
Never ship prose describing tooling the consumer does not receive — ship the runtime.
Never let a package's identity include build artifacts — identity is the source.
